messages:
Maya S.: FYI escalation from Acme-ML — they say their Dedicated pool burn jumped by ~280 GPU-hours overnight but their token/req volume is flat. billing ticket #SUP-3389. attaching dashboards and repro steps below.

James B.: Can you paste the dashboard links and the invoice line?

Maya S.: dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/tenant/acme-ml/dedicated/pools/123/usage - shows 430 reserved hours charged for the week. invoice snippet: INV-2027-09-14 line: Dedicated Reserved Hours 430h ($9,660). Customer expected ~150h.

Maya S.: quick snapshot of traffic: 2.1M tokens/day last 7 days, request rate steady at 12 r/s. No large batch jobs in their account according to logs.

Li Q.: any recent config changes on that pool? autoscale, burst policies, or routing overrides?

Maya S.: customer says they didn't change anything. Pool config (from their support export):
```
pool_id: dedicated-123
reserved_hours_monthly: 720
autoscale: enabled
burst_capacity: 2x
routing: primary-region eu-west-1, fallback global-burst
canary: off
```

Sophie R.: pinging eng-billing and eng-infra — this looks like a metering attribution problem (reserved vs burst attribution). @James B. can you triage? :eyes:

James B.: I started a short-run audit on the metering pipeline. Two hypotheses: 1) burst routed requests incorrectly attributed to reserved bucket; 2) duplicate charge events from retry handling on our side.

James B.: Can we get raw request headers for a sample window? Maya, can you ask Acme to share request IDs around 1791936000–1791960000 (their local timeframe)? we need X-Request-Id + X-Redwood-Pool headers.

Maya S.: Provided sample logs (redacted):
```
[2027-09-12T02:15:03Z] request_id=rcq-7f2 user=acme svc=ingest path=/v1/generate tokens_in=1024 X-Redwood-Pool=dedicated-123 X-Routing=burst
[2027-09-12T02:15:04Z] request_id=rcq-7f3 user=acme svc=ingest path=/v1/generate tokens_in=8 X-Redwood-Pool=dedicated-123 X-Routing=primary
```

Maya S.: They also included an internal job that runs hourly but it should be tiny: 30k tokens per run. nothing that sums to +280h.

James B.: OK, I see mixed routing headers in samples. Two things to check on our side: 1) meter-aggregator dedup window length (could double-count retries), 2) burst-router emitting a reservation-consume event when falling back to reserved hardware. I'll instrument counters.

Li Q.: I'll check the serving logs on dedicated-123 for the period. If serving instances handled requests with NVLink multiplexing, maybe runtime reported active GPU time differently to metering.

deploy-bot: deploy started: metering/patch-1792 -> staging (CI pass).

James B.: quick repro I ran against staging:
1) send 1000 small requests (8–32 tokens) with X-Routing=burst header.
2) simulate a single failing backend response for first attempt, let client retry once.
Result: meter-aggregator emitted 1001 consume events and one reserve-consume event. Looks like retries were double-counted and a fallback path emitted reserve consumption.

Sophie R.: If that's confirmed, customers would see both burst and reserved consumption, inflating billed reserved hours. That matches what Acme reported.

Maya S.: Acme asked for an interim credit if we confirm. They were billed $9.6k on the invoice and estimate actual should be ~$3.3k this period.

James B.: Next steps: roll forward a hotfix to dedupe retries in metering (PR in staging) and disable emitting reserve-consume on transient fallback. If QA passes, patch to prod tonight. I'll prepare a rollback plan.

Li Q.: Also going to reconcile GPU-wallclock reported by runtime vs metering aggregates for last 48h and send CSV to support.

Maya S.: Please add the reconciliation CSV to the ticket and cc me so I can keep the customer updated.

James B.: Action items assigned:
- James B.: patch metering dedupe + disable reserve-consume (in progress)
- Li Q.: runtime vs metering reconciliation CSV (ETA 2h)
- Sophie R.: prepare customer credit calc and legal/finance pre-approval (ETA 4h)
- Maya S.: keep customer patched, collect any more request_ids if they see spikes.

Maya S.: Customer reply: "Thanks — we'll hold off large jobs. can you confirm if this will affect SLA credits?"

Sophie R.: We'll determine financial remediation after we confirm root cause. SLA credits may apply if this meets billing error threshold.

James B.: Update: staging verification passed. dedupe prevents duplicate consume events from retries in our tests. deploying to prod in ~20m.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: metering/patch-1792 -> prod (2027-09-12T06:22:41Z).

Li Q.: reconciliation CSV attached to ticket. Summary: runtime gpu-wallclock shows ~160h used, metering claimed 430h. Difference ~270h traced to duplicated reserve-consume events tied to retry path.

James B.: Prod patch validated. I ran a targeted repro against the prod metering window and no duplicate events observed.

Maya S.: Customer confirmed reserved-hour counter has corrected in their dashboard within 30m. Acme asks for a formal postmortem and a credit for the overcharge.

Sophie R.: I'll draft credit amount and PM for postmortem. assigning to eng-billing for postmortem writeup.

Maya S.: Closing loop with customer now. Thanks team. :tada:
